sum: A short trek from the Melamchi valley to the Hyolmo village of Tarkeghyang, then up through rhododendron forest to the 3,771 m summit of Ama Yangri.

guide.note: The Nepal Tourism Board has required foreign trekkers to hire a licensed guide since April 2023, though checks are inconsistent and on this short route, which most Nepali hikers walk unguided, they are rare. A guide is still worth having for the summit day: the forest trail has unmarked forks, there is no water or shelter above the village, and cloud can cover the top within minutes.

access: Buses and jeeps run from Kathmandu to Timbu, at the head of the Melamchi valley road, in five to six hours. The route passes Melamchi Pul Bazaar and follows the river that flooded in 2021, so it is slow and rough in places. A hired jeep can continue up the dirt road to Tarkeghyang when it is dry.

photo.a: Pink rhododendron flowers and a few prayer flags fill the foreground, with rocky, snow-dusted peaks behind under a band of cloud and a dark forested ridge on the right.
photo.c: Snow peaks and rhododendron in bloom from the summit of Ama Yangri

includes: Langtang National Park permit and TIMS card
meals on standard tiers (not on the cheapest)

permits.name: Langtang National Park entry permit
permits.where: At the park checkpoint in Dhunche on the drive to Syabrubesi, or in advance at the Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu.

permits.name: Trekkers' Information Management System card
permits.where: Only through a registered trekking agency, which applies in the Nepal Tourism Board's online system with your route and your guide's details. Individual trekkers can no longer buy one over the counter.

tips: Carry at least two litres of water and something to eat for the summit day; there is no tea shop on the mountain.
Take a warm jacket, hat and gloves even in spring. You stand still on a windy top at dawn.
Saturdays and public holidays bring large groups from Kathmandu. Go midweek for a quiet summit and an easier choice of rooms.
The summit is a shrine. Walk round the stupa clockwise and take your rubbish back down with you.
Bring cash from Kathmandu; do not count on an ATM once you leave the city.

days.t: Drive to Timbu, walk up to Tarkeghyang
days.note: Leave Kathmandu early for the five to six hour drive through Melamchi Pul Bazaar and up the Melamchi valley. From Timbu a steep trail climbs roughly 1,000 m through terraces and forest to Tarkeghyang, crossing the jeep track several times. Published heights for Timbu differ, so treat that figure as approximate.

days.t: Ama Yangri summit and back to Tarkeghyang
days.note: Start before dawn with a head torch. The trail climbs steadily through oak and rhododendron, steepens on stone steps and comes out on open pasture below the stupa. Allow three to four hours up and two to three down, and carry all your water. Turn round if a headache builds on the upper slopes.

days.t: Walk down to Timbu, drive to Kathmandu
days.note: An easy morning back down to the road at Timbu, then the bus or jeep to Kathmandu. Leave Tarkeghyang by 8 am if you are relying on public transport, as buses down the valley tend to thin out after midday.
